findings.issue: The skip path reads as a pass that proved something. tk2s asserts (linked is None) == (link_skip is not None); linked is set only in the same try whose except sets link_skip, so the two are complementary by construction and tk2s cannot fail on either branch. On a machine that refuses os.symlink (an unprivileged Windows account) tk2l is not emitted at all, the abspath-writer hole this task closes is open again there, and the only trace is a green tk2s whose label is the same fixed sentence on both branches ('either ran ... or was skipped'), with the reason buried in a repr at its tail. The label never says SKIPPED HERE and tk2l never appears under its own id. The repo already has the idiom for exactly this: _harness.skip(check, id, mechanism, absent) (tests/_harness.py:444), used for an os.symlink refusal at tests/test__config.py:3033, tests/test__journal_io.py:2105 and tests/test__output.py:1096; it keeps the case id at the front, says SKIPPED HERE, and fails if the skip is taken on a platform that has the mechanism. The executor's claim that tk2s 'stated the reason' is true only of a repr inside a passing label.
findings.resolution: Drop tk2s. Where the symlink is refused call _harness.skip(check, "tk2l", "os.symlink is refused here (%s)" % link_skip, True), as test__config.py:3033 does, so the lost case keeps its id and reads SKIPPED HERE; keep the tk2l check in the else branch.
